instructions: The night before: rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a bowl of cold water until the water runs almost clear, and cook it in a rice cooker or pot with the water the package calls for. Spread it on a plate to cool, then cover it and keep it in the fridge. Leftover rice you already have works the same.
Take the rice out of the fridge and break up any big clumps with your fingers. You want about 4 cups.
Finely chop half the onion. Cut the 6 oz chicken into 1/2 inch pieces.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring, until it's soft and see-through.
Add the chicken with 1/4 tsp of the salt and a few grinds of pepper. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until there's no pink left when you cut a piece open.
Turn the heat down a little. Stir in 1/3 cup ketchup and the 1 1/2 tsp Worcestershire and cook for about 1 minute, until the sauce thickens and darkens a shade.
Add the rice and fold it through with a spatula, pressing out the clumps, until every grain is orange and hot, about 3 minutes. Stir in the 1/4 cup peas and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook 1 minute.
Taste the rice, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Divide it into 4 portions and cover the pan off the heat.
Make one omelette at a time. Beat 2 of the eggs in a bowl with 1/8 tsp of the salt until no streaks of white are left.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in an 8 to 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. When it foams, pour in the eggs.
Stir the eggs quickly in small circles with chopsticks or a spatula while you shake the pan, for about 30 seconds, until they're soft curds that are still wet on top. Smooth them into an even layer.
Spoon one portion of rice down the middle of the egg in an oval and turn off the heat.
Fold the near side of the egg over the rice, then slide it all toward the far edge of the pan and fold that side over too.
Hold a plate against the far edge of the pan and tip the pan over, so the omurice lands seam side down. Tuck the edges under with a paper towel to make a neat oval.
Make the other three the same way, using 2 eggs, 1/8 tsp salt and 1 tbsp butter each time.
Squeeze a line of ketchup over each one and serve with a green salad.
advance_prep_notes: Cook the rice the night before, or use leftover rice.
method_notes: All the read versions soften onion in butter, cook small pieces of chicken, cook the ketchup in the pan before the rice goes in, and wrap one portion of ketchup rice at a time in a thin, soft omelette. Just One Cookbook and RecipeTin Japan add Worcestershire to the ketchup, and Just One Cookbook strains the eggs and stirs them into soft custardy curds before folding them around the rice. Chopstick Chronicles adds carrot and peas and drapes a flat omelette over the rice. This one follows Just One Cookbook with day-old rice, peas and a stirred omelette for each plate.
